request.spec:
A sheet may name a parent sheet (settings, SETTING_CHANGED key=parent value=<sheet id>; not
dated). A sheet cannot be its own parent, nor name a sheet that has this sheet as an ancestor; and
the parent must be a sheet that exists (has been loaded); each is refused with an error on the
settings. When a grade has no rate in force on a date on this sheet, the parent's rate for that grade
and date is used, then the parent's parent, up to three levels up. Show the parent sheet id on the
screen (nothing when none).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A sheet may name a parent sheet (settings, SETTING_CHANGED key=parent value=<sheet id>; not
dated). A sheet cannot be its own parent, nor name a sheet that has this sheet as an ancestor; and
the parent must be a sheet that exists (has been loaded); each is refused with an error on the
settings. When a grade has no rate in force on a date on this sheet, the parent's rate for that grade
and date is used, then the parent's parent, up to three levels up. Show the parent sheet id on the
screen (nothing when none).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The parent-sheet change is in, but `bin/e2e` still fails 2 of its 4 tests. Both fail on one line: the spec expects the parent to display as the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"` (4 assertions in tests 1 and 3). The screen shows the real parent id instead, e.g. `smvjyedi7g8hp-p`. That looks like a placeholder the spec generator never replaced with `${sheet}-p`, which is how every other line in the spec, including the audit lines, names the parent.

To check everything after that line, I ran a temporary copy of the spec with only those 4 strings changed to `` `${sheet}-p` ``. All 4 tests passed: the refusals, the inherited dues and rollups, `rate-current-*`, and the audit records. I deleted the copy afterwards, and the real spec, `bin/*` and `e2e/support` are untouched. The way to fix it is to correct those 4 strings in the spec. Making the screen print `__SHEET__` would be wrong for real users, so I didn't.

What the change does:

- **Stored data:** `V68__sheet_parent.sql` adds a `parent` column to `sheet`. It isn't dated.
- **Rate lookup** (`RateRepository`): if a grade has no rate on a date on this sheet, it uses the parent's rate, then the grandparent's, up to three levels up. The as-of view does the same with each sheet's rates as they stood on that date. All server-side dues, rollups and statements go through this lookup, so they all pick up the fallback.
- **Saving the setting:** `parent` works like the other settings. A blank value clears it, and saving writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=parent value=<id>`. A new step, `ValidateParent`, runs during the save and refuses three cases: the sheet itself, a sheet that has never been loaded, and a sheet that already has this one as an ancestor. A refusal shows `settings-error` and writes nothing.
- **Front end:**
  - The rates endpoint now returns the parent sheets' rates as well, each tagged with how many levels up it comes from. The screen uses these when the sheet has no rate of its own on a date, and the rate table still lists only the sheet's own rates.
  - The settings form has a `setting-parent` input and shows `setting-parent-current`.
  - `sheet-parent` sits next to "Archived" and is empty when there's no parent.
  - Saving settings now reloads the rates.
